## Architecture & Boundaries
<!-- Repo layout, module ownership, how modules communicate, forbidden couplings.

## API
<!-- Read by: api-designer (and both implementers).
     Style (REST/GraphQL/RPC), where contracts live (OpenAPI files, shared
     types), versioning policy, standard error shape, pagination pattern. -->

## Conventions
<!-- Identifier language, naming, ID strategy (e.g. UUID v7), money/quantity types
     and precision, timezone policy, error-handling idiom.
     Working language: what language agents use for reports, plans, specs, and
     discussion with the user (e.g. "Spanish for reports and discussion; English
     for code, identifiers, comments, and commit messages"). Omit for English. -->

## Non-negotiables
<!-- The "never do" list. Security, compliance, data rules. Every agent enforces
     these; code-reviewer blocks on them. e.g.:
     - Never store card numbers anywhere, including logs.
     - Every query is tenant-scoped.
     - No physical deletes of business documents.
     - Secrets only via Key Vault. -->

## Security
<!-- Read by: security-expert (and everyone via Non-negotiables).
     Auth mechanism (who authenticates how, where sessions/tokens live), secret
     store, compliance regime (PCI, GDPR, ...), trust boundaries (which inputs
     are untrusted - public API, supplier portal, file uploads), sensitive-data
     classes that must never appear in logs/errors, dependency audit command
     (e.g. `npm audit`, `dotnet list package --vulnerable`). -->

## UI / Design System
<!-- Read by: ux-designer, ui-implementer.
     Design system + version (e.g. Metronic 8.2.6, Tailwind + shadcn/ui), styling
     rules (custom CSS allowed? overrides?), icon policy, i18n mechanism,
     shared-component location, permission/visibility mechanism, authoritative
     design docs to read. -->

## Database
<!-- Read by: db-engineer (and implementers for persistence conventions).
     Engine + version, schema location, migration policy (canonical file vs
     numbered migrations vs framework tool), standard columns every table needs,
     seed location + policy, how to validate against a clean DB, schema doc that
     must stay in sync. -->

## Testing
<!-- Read by: test-writer.
     Frameworks, integration policy (real DB via Testcontainers? mocks where?),
     test location + naming convention, how to run the suite, priority order for
     what must be tested. -->

## Performance
<!-- Read by: performance-engineer.
     Budgets/SLOs (endpoint latency, page weight, job durations), expected load
     profile (users, rows, requests/s), profiling tools available. "None" means
     findings are reported as absolute numbers. -->

## Deployment
<!-- Read by: devops-engineer.
     CI system + pipeline file locations, environments and how code reaches
     them, IaC location/tool, container/image conventions, CI secret mechanism,
     where env vars are documented. -->

## Review
<!-- Read by: code-reviewer, on top of its universal checklist.
     Project-specific BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR criteria and the base branch to
     diff against. -->

## Docs
<!-- Read by: doc-keeper.
     Files that must stay in sync with code: decision log (numbering scheme),
     open-questions ledger, architecture docs, backlog. "None" is a valid answer. -->
